nt_the_ledge_assembly.blurb: A small, multi-level cliff right in town, just off the trail that loops Frame Lake near the Legislative Assembly. It is purely a bouldering spot with 13 problems packed close together, mostly V0 with a few up to V3. Many of the lines lean slightly past vertical and the styles vary, which makes it a handy quick session without leaving the city. The side path to the wall is short, so the walk is only a minute or two from the main lakeside trail.

nt_main_wall_3.blurb: The main cliff of the Burwash/Big Crack area, a small waterfront crag a few kilometres north of Dettah across the bay from Yellowknife, and the city's busiest climbing spot. Twelve routes, mostly bolted sport lines with a couple of trad cracks and top ropes, covering roughly 5.6 to 5.11. The heart of the grade range sits in the 5.8 to 5.10 band, and a popular short bolted line serves as many climbers' first 5.10. Routes are short, around 35 feet, so it suits quick laps and newer leaders. A clear forest trail leads in from the road.

nt_muskeg_boulders.blurb: A bouldering zone in the Hidden Valley near Cameron Falls outside Yellowknife, the second cluster you meet after the Staircase Boulders and Dominoes on the right-hand side. A single long wall runs uphill into the trees, with several detached blocks nearby. Eleven problems range from V0 to V3, mostly short at around 10 to 15 feet, with a clean soft landing on some and an awkward talus landing on others. Expect a bushwhack to get there, damp ground underfoot and rock that is still fairly vegetated; tread lightly on the plants.

nt_power_line_cliff.blurb: A short, bouldery cliff at the Ravine on Yellowknife's north side, tucked behind a stand of trees with a power line cut running in front of it. Eleven climbs, mostly boulder problems from V0 to V2, plus a couple of trad lines in the 5.7 to 5.10 range. Walls are low, around 10 feet, with good edges and big holds on the topouts, so a spotter is welcome. It sits a short stroll from the waterfront bouldering and makes an easy add-on to a visit to the Ravine.
nt_power_line_cliff.parking_note: Use the ski club parking lot, then follow the rock knobs toward the waterfront and turn left.
